content: Reduced PDH activity or flux has never been directly measured in WWOX-deficient human neural cells; the PDH hypothesis is untested, not refuted.

content: Hypothesis that WWOX loss impairs pyruvate oxidation rests wholly on extrapolation from a cancer/MEF framework; each link is published but the chain was assembled only in tumour-suppressor biology.

content: WWOX, via its first WW domain, interacts with HIF1a and modulates level/transactivation; Wwox-deficient cells show raised HIF1a, glucose uptake, glycolysis, reduced mitochondrial respiration (Warburg-like) and elevated GLUT1.
anchor: L17, L50, L86, L88, L101 Finding 1
note: Cancer cell lines and MEFs. Audit: the same paper reports higher Pdk1 transcript in KO cells and higher serum lactate in KO mice (Suppl Fig S2A); not in the report's text

content: HIF-1 directly transactivates PDK1; PDK1 inactivates PDH (pyruvate to acetyl-CoA), suppressing TCA flux and shunting glucose carbon to lactate.
note: Non-WWOX hypoxia datum in HIF-1alpha null cells. Audit: a WWOX-specific PDK1 transcript datum exists in PMID 25012504 (see E04/E39); PDH activity and phosphorylation not measured there

content: Model A predicted chain: WWOX loss -> HIF1a up -> PDK1 up -> PDH-E1a(Ser293) phosphorylation up -> PDH flux down -> lactate up; DCA would act at the PDK step.
note: Labelled EXTRAPOLATED, never measured in neurons

content: Wwox-null mice succumb to lethal hypoglycemia early in life.
cited_source: succumb to a lethal hypoglycemia early in life (PMID 25012504)

content: Mouse hypoglycemia is consistent with the excess glycolytic glucose consumption the HIF1a-PDK1 axis would predict.

content: Full-text review of the dismech WOREE YAML finds no metabolic, PDH or mitochondrial pathophysiology node, so no disorder-specific prior constrains the hypothesis.
note: Report says full text reviewed

content: Human WOREE clinical phenotype lacks lactic acidosis and hypoglycemia, which define genuine PDH-pathway disease (PDCD); the dismech phenotype set contains neither.
note: Source for the absence is the dismech entry, not a clinical series

content: The only metabolic phenotype in the dismech entry is Wwox-null mouse hypoglycemia, which curators note has no direct counterpart in the human course (rescue data).
note: Identifier written with colon, no space

content: Absence of human lactic acidosis argues against a gross systemic PDH-flux block; any neural defect, if real, is likely subtle and cell-autonomous or compartment-restricted, not excluded.
note: Hedged: subtle defect not excluded

content: In differentiated human SH-SY5Y neurons under high-glucose stress, WWOX activation (Tyr33 phosphorylation) rose and drove mitochondrial dysfunction, ROS and death; pharmacological WWOX inhibition (Zfra1-31) restored mitochondrial homeostasis and viability.
note: Human neuronal cell line, metabolic-stress paradigm, not developmental null

content: The neuronal WWOX-mitochondria relationship is opposite in sign to the cancer/MEF model; WWOX effect is cell-context dependent and the Warburg model cannot be transplanted onto neurons untested.

content: Drosophila neurons, Wwox knockdown in Abeta42 background: elevated Ldh expression and lactate, driven by Atf4; "genetic reduction of Ldh rescued locomotor deficits".
note: In vivo, fly, Abeta42-sensitised, 2026 per report

content: Neuronal Wwox overexpression in the fly reduced amyloid burden and reversed the transcriptional changes.
note: Side result. Added from the audited source text (not report content): the paper's Discussion says the Wwox-overexpression rescue occurs without Ldh or 2-hydroxyglutarate falling, which limits reading Ldh as the general mediator of Wwox effects

content: Fly data are the first direct neural in vivo evidence that Wwox loss diverts pyruvate to lactate and that correcting pyruvate handling is therapeutically relevant; pyruvate metabolism is genuinely dysregulated by Wwox loss in neurons.
note: Stated as net effect despite caveats

content: Fly qualification (i): the measured node is LDH expression, lactate and LDH epistasis, not PDH activity, E1a phosphorylation, PDK expression or pyruvate-to-acetyl-CoA flux.
note: Decisive for the question per report

content: Fly qualification (ii): driver is ATF4 (integrated stress response), not HIF1a-PDK1.
note: Merged with Model B note on driver

content: Fly qualifications (iii)-(iv): Drosophila not human cells, and phenotype characterised in an Abeta42-sensitised background rather than pure developmental Wwox loss.
note: Species and context gap

content: Model B: Wwox loss -> ATF4 up -> LDH up -> lactate up (pyruvate to lactate, not blocked oxidation); lowering LDH rescues; PDK/PDH role untested. Newly favoured as the better-supported neural abnormality.

content: Evidence reorients the plausibly actionable node away from PDK/PDH toward LDH and the integrated stress response, making empiric PDK inhibition even less well targeted.
note: LDH named as genetically validated rescue node (L104)

content: A PDH defect is unproven and arguably unlikely to be the dominant lesion; the better-supported neural abnormality is an ISR-driven LDH shift.
note: Honest synthesis in report's words

content: Dichloroacetate (DCA), prototypical PDK inhibitor that reactivates PDH, assessed as candidate intervention.
note: Compound named; no dose given in report except trial dose in E25

content: RCT of DCA in MELAS (25 mg/kg/day): 30 randomised; 19 taken off study medication (15 DCA, 4 placebo), 17 of those 19 for onset or worsening of neuropathy; stopped early, no efficacy benefit. Report reads 17/19 as patients affected.
note: Audit correction: the report's '17 of 19 patients' uses 19 as the trial population (denominator misreading); 17 is a share of discontinuations; the abstract does not split the 17 by arm. Dose is a source fact

content: Long-term DCA in congenital lactic acidosis (incl. PDH-complex deficiency) was generally tolerated and normalised blood lactate, but still reduced nerve conduction in some patients.
note: Mixed: benefit in true PDH disease plus neurotoxicity

content: HIF1-PDK1 switch is cytoprotective: forced PDK1 expression in hypoxic cells "increases ATP levels, attenuates hypoxic ROS generation, and rescues these cells from hypoxia-induced apoptosis".
note: Hypoxic non-neuronal cells

content: Reactivating PDH with DCA could remove a protective anti-ROS adaptation and raise ROS in cells already undergoing neurodegeneration.
note: Transfer from hypoxia cell biology to WWOX neurons

content: WWOX-DEE has independent non-metabolic seizure drivers: Wnt/GSK-3b dysregulation (lithium abolishes PTZ-induced seizures in Wwox-/- mice) and cortical E/I imbalance; a metabolic intervention may not touch the seizure mechanism.
note: Lithium result stated without citation

content: DCA is justified only under a narrow, currently unsatisfied condition: a proven PDK-driven PDH block with demonstrated residual PDH capacity to reactivate.
note: Also title of Finding 2: conditionally justified at best

content: Ketogenic diet (KD): ketone-derived acetyl-CoA enters the TCA cycle downstream of PDH, bypassing the block and needing no residual PDH activity.
note: Mechanism stated as general

content: In a PDH complex deficiency (PDCD) cohort KD "was effective in both prenatal- and postnatal-onset disease"; seizure frequency fell in 8/9 (89%) with epilepsy.
note: Genuine PDCD, not WWOX

content: PDCD is an "absolute indication" for KD among drug-resistant genetic epilepsies.
note: Not WWOX

content: KD lowered lactate "in all patients with PDCD" in a paediatric inborn-errors-of-metabolism series.
note: Not WWOX

content: If a neural PDH defect were confirmed, KD is the mechanism-matched, lower-risk option (no residual PDH needed, no DCA neuropathy); WWOX-DEE is a drug-resistant genetic epilepsy where KD is an established adjunct.
note: Conditional on unproven defect; KD in WWOX-DEE itself not cited

content: Neurons rely primarily on OXPHOS and TCA to sustain synaptic activity; astrocytes predominantly engage glycolysis producing lactate that fuels neurons via the astrocyte-neuron lactate shuttle (ANLS).
note: Review; general brain metabolism

content: when mitochondrial function is impaired, cells undergo metabolic reprogramming toward aerobic glycolysis, leading to lactate accumulation.
note: Generic mitochondrial-impairment consequence

content: Brain/CSF lactate is multi-sourced (astrocytic glycolysis, seizure activity, any mitochondrial impairment, LDH up-regulation) and does not localise a defect to neuronal PDH; so the decisive assay must be cell-type-resolved and flux-specific.
note: Bulk lactate called uninterpretable (L120)
